Yudhishthira's procession includes Dhritarashtra, Gandhari, Kunti (also referred to as Pritha), his brothers (the Pandavas), Krishna (also referred to as Janardana, son of Vasudeva), Vidura, and many kings, attendants, and priests.

attributes.relationships: Yudhishthira leads the royal family and allies to honor Bhishma.

extraction_text: The procession arrives at Kurukshetra where Bhishma lies on his bed of arrows, surrounded by sages including Vyasa (also referred to as son of Parashara), Narada, and Devala, as well as surviving kings.

attributes.scene: Bhishma's deathbed surrounded by sages and royalty

extraction_text: Yudhishthira and his brothers descend from their chariots, pay respects to Bhishma (their grandfather) and the sages led by Vyasa.

attributes.relationships: Grandfather-grandsons; reverence to sages

extraction_text: Yudhishthira addresses the lying Bhishma, announcing his arrival with the funeral fire and all required preparations, and asks Bhishma what he should do for him.

attributes.purpose: To perform the funeral rites as instructed

extraction_text: Bhishma opens his eyes, sees the gathered Bharata clan, takes Yudhishthira's arm, and speaks, expressing joy at their arrival and noting that the sun has turned northward, marking the awaited time.

attributes.supernatural_element: Timing based on the sun's northward turn (divine or astrological sign)
attributes.state: Bhishma has been lying on his arrow bed for 58 days

extraction_text: Bhishma informs Yudhishthira that the month of Magha has arrived with three-quarters remaining in the bright fortnight.
Bhishma addresses Dhritarashtra, praising his knowledge of dharma, Vedas, and respect for Brahmins.
Bhishma advises Dhritarashtra not to grieve, as events are destined, and reminds him of divine stories heard from Vyasa.
Bhishma tells Dhritarashtra to protect the Pandavas equally under dharma, noting Yudhishthira's obedience and the Kauravas' flawed nature.
Bhishma turns to Krishna, praising him as a divine being worshipped by gods and asuras, and requests permission to leave the world.

supernatural_elements: Krishna identified as divine, worshipped by gods and asuras

extraction_text: Bhishma asks Krishna to protect the Pandavas, recalling his past advice to Duryodhana about aligning with Krishna for victory.

relationships: Bhishma as former advisor to Duryodhana

extraction_text: Bhishma recounts Duryodhana's refusal to heed his advice for peace with the Pandavas, leading to war and death.
Bhishma reveals knowledge from sages Narada and Vyasa that Nara and Narayana (Arjuna and Krishna) have incarnated on Earth.

relationships: Krishna and Arjuna as divine incarnations (Narayana and Nara)
Narada and Vyasa as sources of wisdom
supernatural_elements: Krishna and Arjuna identified as ancient sages incarnated

extraction_text: Krishna grants Bhishma permission to leave for the divine world, praising his virtue and control over death.

supernatural_elements: Bhishma's ability to control death due to virtue

extraction_text: Bhishma addresses the Pandavas led by Dhritarashtra after Krishna's response.
A character prepares to give up his life and gives final instructions to his friends.

relationships: Bhishma as elder/teacher to Yudhishthira and friends
key_points: Bhishma instructs them to pursue truth and respect Brahmins

extraction_text: Bhishma embraces all his friends and gives specific advice to Yudhishthira.

key_points: Bhishma emphasizes respect for wise Brahmins and teachers
